subject: SURF-008
reason: Re-judged after the header fix. Section headers are now sentence case semibold in the secondary tier, which is the rule the design states and argues for, and they recede under the row titles as intended. Three differences remain, and all three are the build carrying MORE than the design rather than less: a title block (icon, 'Proctor', two paragraphs) the design does not draw; grant rows using a tick glyph with the state on a second line where the design uses a left icon, a description and a right-hand pill; and a green 'Ready. Every permission Proctor needs is granted.' sentence beneath a section header that already carries a Ready pill. Each is a composition decision rather than a rule the design argues, and closing them means deleting explanation, so they are left for a decision rather than changed in passing.

subject: SURF-009
reason: Same window, same first slide, different composition. The build leads with a three-segment progress bar and the heading 'What Proctor does'; the design leads with a bordered icon and the heading 'A model can test this Mac'. The design carries three capability chips (READS accessibility tree, READS window pixels, DRIVES two planes) which the build replaces with two paragraphs and a 'Two permissions, asked once' callout. Both offer Skip setup and Set up permissions with the same emphasis, so the decision the slide asks for is unchanged. This is PRO-0067's A3, carried and now measured.

subject: SURF-010
reason: The capture is Proctor's character in the menu bar, cropped to the AXExtrasMenuBar frame this process reported, and it is that character rather than any other application's status item. Frame-exact comparison is not meaningful here and is not claimed: the character animates, the reference is the idle-0 frame, and a live capture lands on whichever frame was drawn. What is settled is identity and placement, which is what this surface's case rests on.
